Topics · Is there a God?

How can I tell for myself what is true?

A method to run alone: leave the crowd, sort claims by kind, write what would change your mind. And its limit.

Part 1 of 3

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍ ۖ أَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا۟ ۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَّكُم بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allāh, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.

Quran · Saba 34:46

Start by removing what is not evidence. A crowd is not evidence: people believe things together because they are together, and that applies to believers, to atheists and to anyone's online community. So the first step in any honest inquiry is to get out of the room. Think alone, or with one other person you trust. Whatever you conclude there is more likely to be yours. That is a method, and you can use it on this app too.

A question for you

Who is hardest for you to think apart from?

If you sayMy family and the people I grew up with.
ThenThen this is your first step, and it is an inner one that nobody sees.
If you sayThe people I read now.
ThenThat is rare honesty. The crowd is not always the old one.
If you sayMyself: what I want to be true.
ThenThat runs in both directions, and it is the hardest one to send out of the room.
If you sayNo one. I think freely.
ThenPerhaps. The question of how you would know that stays open, and it is a good one to ask of any of us.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

Next, sort the claims, because they cannot all be checked the same way. Some can be tested against the world: does this text contradict itself or known fact? Some can be reasoned about: does what begins need a source? Some can be weighed like a court weighs a witness: who was this man, what did he gain? Some cannot be checked from here at all: what follows death. Be strict with each kind, and be equally strict with whatever you believe instead.

A question for you

What kind of knowing would you accept on a question like this?

If you sayA proof, like mathematics.
ThenThat is a high bar. Most of what you live by does not reach it, the opposite view included. Nothing here will claim it.
If you sayWhat would satisfy a court: evidence adding up in one direction.
ThenThat is the nearest thing that can be offered here, and you decide whether it adds up.
If you sayA direct experience of my own.
ThenThat is what comes next, and it has its limit.
If you sayI don't think anything would be enough.
ThenThat is a possible position. It is worth asking whether it is a result or an earlier decision.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى ۖ قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا ۚ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allāh] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allāh] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself.[107] Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise."

Translator's notes

[107] i.e., train them to come to you on command.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:260

Translation

As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were. Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.” Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.

Original · Ancient Greek

καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα· ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου· καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

Romans · 4:17-21

World English Bible

﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

Original · Hebrew

וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּמָצָ֑אתָ כִּ֣י תִדְרְשֶׁ֔נּוּ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 4:29

World English Bible

The last kind of test is the least tidy. Some claims of religion are about a relationship, and a relationship cannot be tested from outside. So some people try it: they speak to whoever may be there, honestly, for a while, and watch. Be clear about what this can and cannot do. If nothing happens, that is real and does not make you insincere. The verse sets no date. If something happens, it is not proof for anyone else. It is one more thing to weigh, and it is yours.

A question for you

Which best describes your experience of this?

If you sayI tried for a long time and found nothing.
ThenThat is real, and this page does not explain it by anything in you. A whole question takes it up.
If you sayI never tried, and I don't plan to.
ThenThat is your choice. All the other routes stay open to you.
If you sayI felt something, and I don't know what it was.
ThenYou do not need to name it now, and no one will decide it for you.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 360-361

Max Müller, 1881
